assessment.nobel_worthiness: Created a coherent, rigorous field of modern political economics. It links constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy through formal theory and careful empirics, and it has shaped macro, public and development economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini built the constitutional and electoral-rule programme and its systematic empirical testing. Besley, with Persson and others, developed the state-capacity and development-oriented strand. The three-person trio is natural, though other contributors such as Acemoglu and Alesina sit adjacent. Acemoglu is already recognised for related institutions work.
assessment.maturity: The work spans more than three decades, with core results well replicated and absorbed into the standard toolkit. It has been in the Nobel conversation for a long time.
uncertainties: Possible perceived overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity.
Boundary of credit with Alesina (deceased) and other political-economy contributors.
Some causal claims in the empirical constitutions literature rest on cross-country identification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity framework transformed international trade by explaining selection, exporting and the within-industry gains from trade. It also changed how trade policy and welfare are quantified.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to the export-versus-FDI choice and broader applications. Redding's quantitative contributions are real but more derivative of the core idea. Two names capture the core credit cleanly.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of extensive theoretical, empirical and quantitative follow-up. The framework is now canonical in graduate teaching.
uncertainties: Helpman also appears on another trade-politics candidate, so credit could be split across the trade field.
Empirical contributors (Bernard, Jensen and others) are not on this ballot and are an alternative attribution.
Trade was recognised in 2008 (Krugman), which may affect field balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins modern monetary-policy analysis and central-bank practice worldwide. It combines microfounded price setting, policy rules and welfare-based analysis.
assessment.attribution: The credit is highly diffuse. Calvo supplied time-dependent pricing, Taylor the rule and staggered contracts, and Woodford the integrated theory of interest and prices. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others made major contributions, and a cap of three laureates forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of use in policy institutions. Its performance in the post-2020 inflation episode has been debated but has not displaced the framework.
uncertainties: Large unresolved attribution problem across at least eight credited names.
Some of the credited names are contested relative to the framework's later estimated-DSGE strand.
Debate on the framework's adequacy after the 2021-23 inflation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint credit-cycle mechanism explains how small shocks are amplified and persist through asset prices and borrowing limits. It is foundational for macro-finance and for post-2008 policy thinking.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) are the clear originators of the collateral-driven amplification mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator tradition, which Bernanke (2022) was already recognised for. Two names are the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: A long-established base with a dominant role in quantitative macro-finance models and ongoing use in crisis analysis.
uncertainties: Possible perceived overlap with the 2022 prize for banks and financial crises.
Empirical validation of the precise amplification channel is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed how misallocation of inputs across heterogeneous firms can account for large cross-country productivity and income differences. It built a tractable, measurable bridge between micro data and development and growth accounting.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) are the central measurement contribution. Restuccia and Rogerson developed a closely related and contemporaneous framework, and Restuccia is credited here. Priority and credit are shared in a way that makes the laureate set uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Highly influential for about fifteen years. Some measurement critiques remain, but the framework is widely used in development and macro.
uncertainties: Credit relative to Restuccia and Rogerson, who is not credited here.
Measurement error and the interpretation of dispersion in marginal products as pure misallocation.
The prize on growth was awarded in 2018 and 2025, which may affect field balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reshaped understanding of how technology and trade shocks alter labour demand, task content, wage inequality and local labour markets. The China-shock evidence changed both academic and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the core authors of the trade-shock evidence. The task-based technology strand has Autor, Katz and others, so combining the strands creates a crowded and partly distinct contribution set.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of work with strong replication. Debates about interpretation and persistence continue, but the empirical findings are well established.
uncertainties: Katz, Goldin, Acemoglu and Restrepo overlap on the task and technology side.
Whether the committee sees the China-shock work as one discovery or two.
Some magnitudes remain contested in the later literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining and its market extensions gave a strategic foundation for bargaining outcomes. They are widely used across labour, industrial organisation, macro search and political economy.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the decisive contribution. Wolinsky, with Rubinstein, extended it to decentralised markets. Binmore's work on the strategic and axiomatic link is important but secondary in credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and canonical in textbooks. A strong case on lasting impact, though it may seem a classical result relative to more recent topical work.
uncertainties: Perceived overlap with the earlier game-theory and mechanism-design prizes.
Binmore's role in the credit assignment.
Applied impact is largely indirect, through the models built on it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Constructed long-run top-income and wealth series from tax data, reshaping the empirical study of inequality, tax policy and offshore wealth. The contribution is in measurement and data, with large policy and scholarly influence.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez established the top-income series methodology, and Zucman extended it to wealth and offshore holdings. Credit among the three is well defined, though the data collaboration is broad, including Atkinson (deceased).
assessment.maturity: Two decades of influence, with substantial replication of the basic series. The theoretical and policy interpretations of r > g and wealth taxation are contested and are separate from the measurement contribution.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over the treatment of capital income, survey versus tax data and distributional national accounts.
The extent to which the prize would be seen as rewarding measurement versus contested policy views.
Atkinson's deceased status for the early income-distribution work.
